title: The Moon height map is the right way round
criterion: Known craters are low, Mons Malapert is high, and only one orientation of the map fits
summary: There are 8 possible ways to orient the map. 1 of them puts all 7 known craters and mountains in the right place: the one that the app uses. With the first threshold (1.0 km for craters), 0 of 8 fitted. The report gives the history.
details: Contrast in km, positive = as expected (ring mean minus disc mean for craters, disc minus ring for the massif).
Disc = central 40% of the radius, ring = 1.3 to 1.8 radii, sampled every 320 m in the projected plane. "off-DEM" = more than 10% of the area outside the data.
| Axis convention | Haworth | Shoemaker | Faustini | de Gerlache | Cabeus | Shackleton | Mons Malapert | Smallest | All >= 0.5 km |

**Criterion history (read this).** The first run used thresholds set in advance: depression >= 1 km, high >= 0.5 km. Result: 0 of 8 conventions fit, because de Gerlache gave a contrast of 0.80 km under our convention. The criterion was then revised, after seeing these numbers (so post hoc), to one threshold of 0.5 km for every feature. Exactly one convention (ours) fits for any threshold above 0.07 km up to 0.80 km, so the result does not hinge on the exact 0.5 km. The original 1.0 km lies outside that range. Why de Gerlache is only +0.8 km (its ring may lie on low ground) was not investigated.
Targets (IAU Gazetteer, centre latitude and east longitude as published):
| Feature | Gazetteer id | Lat | Lon | Diameter (km) | Expected |

Not covered by V0: the DEM vertical datum (section 11 item 6). A constant offset changes a skyline only through the sphere radius, relative size about delta / R (section 6), so it does not block the build.
Latitude in the Gazetteer is labelled planetographic; on the Moon's reference sphere that equals planetocentric.
